implementation_notes: Java supports the full set: interfaces for abstractions, constructor injection, `sealed interface`/`sealed class` to close a hierarchy for extension, and default methods for interface evolution. Prefer records for immutable abstractions. Make package-private the default visibility so that public surface stays minimal (ISP at package level).
idiom_name: interface + constructor injection + sealed types + records
pitfalls: Field injection via `@Autowired` on fields bypasses constructor guarantees and hides required dependencies.
Interfaces declared in the implementing package rather than the consuming one.
Deep class hierarchies that exist for code reuse break LSP; the JDK collections API is the classic counterexample.
Default methods used to bolt behaviour onto an interface mix policy into the contract of every implementor.
